readings.text: 26 In the sixth month of Elizabeth's pregnancy, God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth, a town in Galilee, 27 to a virgin pledged to be married to a man named Joseph, a descendant of David. The virgin's name was Mary. 28 The angel went to her and said, "Greetings, you who are highly favored! The Lord is with you." 29 Mary was greatly troubled at his words and wondered what kind of greeting this might be. 30 But the angel said to her, "Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favor with God. 31 You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to call him Jesus. 32 He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, 33 and he will reign over Jacob's descendants forever; his kingdom will never end."

34 "How will this be," Mary asked the angel, "since I am a virgin?" 35 The angel answered, "The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the holy one to be born will be called the Son of God. 36 Even Elizabeth your relative is going to have a child in her old age, and she who was said to be unable to conceive is in her sixth month. 37 For no word from God will ever fail." 38 "I am the Lord's servant," Mary answered. "May your word to me be fulfilled." Then the angel left her.
14 Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel.

story: Last week we learned that long before Jesus was born, God promised to send a Savior. This week we see God begin to keep that promise in a very special way.

In a little town called Nazareth lived a young woman named Mary. She was pledged to be married to a man named Joseph, who came from King David's family. One day God sent the angel Gabriel, a messenger from heaven, to visit her.

Gabriel said, "Greetings, you who are highly favored! The Lord is with you." Mary was troubled and wondered what this greeting meant. But Gabriel said, "Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favor with God." Favor means God's kindness and blessing, a gift Mary did not earn.

Then Gabriel gave the big news: Mary would have a baby boy, and she was to name him Jesus. He would be great, he would be called the Son of the Most High, and he would sit on King David's throne. His kingdom would never end. That sounds just like the promised King from Isaiah 9 we learned about last week!

Mary asked, "How will this be?" She was not married yet. Gabriel explained that the Holy Spirit would come on her and the power of God would make it happen, so the holy one born would be called the Son of God. Long before, Isaiah had promised, "The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel." Gabriel also told her that her relative Elizabeth, who was old, was going to have a baby too. Then he said, "For no word from God will ever fail."

Mary answered, "I am the Lord's servant. May your word to me be fulfilled." She trusted God and said yes to his plan, even though it was hard to understand. Next week we will hear what God told Joseph in a dream.
weeks.enochLine: An angel told Mary, "You will have a baby named Jesus!" Nothing is too hard for God!
enochActivities: Activity: Angel message. A parent pretends to be Gabriel and whispers, "Do not be afraid! You will have a baby named Jesus!" Enoch runs to tell everyone in the family, "Jesus is coming!"

Yes, Lord game: a parent says a simple helpful job ("Please pick up one toy"), and Enoch answers like Mary, "Yes, I'll help!" and does it. Say together, "Mary said yes to God!" Paw Patrol touch: when Ryder calls, the pups say, "Ready for action!" Mary was ready for God's plan.
elijahQuestions: Which angel did God send to Nazareth, and who did he visit (verses 26–27)?
What did the angel tell Mary not to be (verse 30)?
What name was Mary supposed to give her baby (verse 31)?
How long would Jesus' kingdom last (verse 33)?
jordynQuestions: Gabriel said Jesus would be called "the Son of the Most High" and would get "the throne of his father David" (verse 32). How does that connect to the Isaiah 9:6–7 promise from last week?
Mary asked, "How will this be?" (verse 34). How was her question different from doubting God, and how did Gabriel answer it (verses 35–37)?
Mary said, "I am the Lord's servant. May your word to me be fulfilled" (verse 38). What did saying yes to God's plan probably cost her, and why do you think she said it anyway?
weeks.jordynApplication: God doesn't send angels to us the way he did to Mary, but he does speak to us in his Word, the Bible. This week, when you read something God asks of you, like being kind to someone who isn't kind to you, telling the truth, or obeying your parents right away, try answering like Mary: "I am the Lord's servant." Pick one thing that feels hard, at school, at volleyball, or at home, and say yes to God in it this week. Remember verse 37: no word from God will ever fail.
elijahAnswers: The angel Gabriel. He visited Mary, who was pledged to be married to Joseph (verses 26–27).
Afraid. The angel said, "Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favor with God" (verse 30).
Jesus (verse 31).
Forever. "His kingdom will never end" (verse 33).
jordynAnswers: Isaiah promised a son who would reign on David's throne forever with no end to his kingdom (Isaiah 9:7). Gabriel says the same about Jesus: the throne of David and a kingdom that will never end (verses 32–33). Jesus is the promised King.

Mary believed but asked how, since she was a virgin (verse 34). Gabriel did not scold her; he explained that the Holy Spirit and the power of the Most High would do it (verse 35), pointed to Elizabeth as proof (verse 36), and said no word from God will ever fail (verse 37).
Her plans for her life and wedding would change, and people might not understand. She said yes because she trusted that God was good and that his word would come true (verses 37–38).
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week what hard thing she chose to say yes to God about and how it went, and notice when she obeys or helps without being asked twice.
weeks.prayer: Dear God, thank you for sending the angel Gabriel to tell Mary that Jesus was coming. Thank you that Jesus is the Son of God and the King whose kingdom will never end. Thank you that no word from you will ever fail. Help us trust you like Mary did and say, "We are your servants," even when your plan is hard to understand. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2
dailies.focus: God sent the angel Gabriel to tell Mary she would have a son named Jesus, the King whose kingdom will never end.
dailies.verse: You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to call him Jesus.
dailies.enoch: Say with a parent, "The angel said, 'Do not be afraid!' Jesus is coming!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 27, whose family did Joseph come from?
dailies.elijahAnswer: David's family. Joseph was "a descendant of David" (verse 27).
dailies.jordyn: Gabriel said Mary had "found favor with God" (verse 30). What does favor mean, and did Mary earn it?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Favor means God's kindness and blessing. Mary did not earn it; God chose to give it, the same way God shows grace to us. That is why she could stop being afraid (verse 30).
dailies.action: Read verses 30–33 together. Each person names one thing Gabriel said about Jesus.
dailies.prayer: Lord God, thank you for sending Gabriel with good news to Mary. Thank you that Jesus is the Son of the Most High and the King whose kingdom will never end. When we feel afraid, help us remember that you are with us. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Nazareth was a small, ordinary town in Galilee, and Mary was a young woman pledged to be married to Joseph, a man from King David's family. God sent the angel Gabriel to her with a message. Gabriel said she was highly favored, which means God had chosen to show her his kindness, and that the Lord was with her. Mary was troubled, so Gabriel told her not to be afraid. Then he told her she would have a son and name him Jesus, who would be called the Son of the Most High and would sit on David's throne forever. This is the promise from Isaiah 9 we learned last week starting to come true: God always keeps his promises.
dailies.enochActivity: Put on a pretend crown and march around the room. Say, "Jesus is the King, and his kingdom will never end!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 28, what did the angel say to Mary first? How did she feel (verse 29)?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: "Greetings, you who are highly favored! The Lord is with you" (verse 28). Mary was greatly troubled and wondered what kind of greeting this was (verse 29).
dailies.jordyn2: Verses 32–33 list several things about Jesus. Which ones show he is more than an ordinary king? Why would that matter to God's people who had waited so long?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: He would be called the Son of the Most High (verse 32), and he would reign forever with a kingdom that never ends (verse 33). No ordinary king lives forever. It mattered because this was the King God had promised through the prophets, and he would never lose his throne.
dailies.passageText: 26 In the sixth month of Elizabeth’s pregnancy, God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth, a town in Galilee, 27 to a virgin pledged to be married to a man named Joseph, a descendant of David. The virgin’s name was Mary. 28 The angel went to her and said, “Greetings, you who are highly favored! The Lord is with you.” 29 Mary was greatly troubled at his words and wondered what kind of greeting this might be. 30 But the angel said to her, “Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favor with God. 31 You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to call him Jesus. 32 He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, 33 and he will reign over Jacob’s descendants forever; his kingdom will never end.”

dailies.label: Day 3
dailies.focus: Nothing God says will ever fail, so Mary trusted him and said yes.
dailies.verse: For no word from God will ever fail.
dailies.enoch: Play "Too hard for God?" A parent asks, "Is it too hard for God to make the stars?" Enoch shouts, "No! Nothing is too hard for God!"
dailies.elijah: Game: Too hard for God? Take turns naming something really hard (moving a mountain, making a baby for old Elizabeth, making the sun). Everyone answers, "No word from God will ever fail!" Then: what question did Mary ask the angel in verse 34?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "How will this be," since she was a virgin (verse 34). She wanted to know how God would do it.
dailies.jordyn: Gabriel said, "For no word from God will ever fail" (verse 37). Why do you think he told Mary about Elizabeth right before saying that?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Elizabeth's baby was proof that God can do what seems impossible (verse 36). If God could do that for Elizabeth, Mary could trust that his word to her would come true too (verse 37).
dailies.action: Play the "Too hard for God?" game, then read verse 37 together and say it in your loudest voice.
dailies.prayer: Almighty God, thank you that no word from you will ever fail. When something feels impossible, help us remember Elizabeth and Mary and trust you. Like Mary, help us say, "We are your servants," and believe what you say. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: After Gabriel's big news, Mary asked a real question: "How will this be?" She was not married yet, so she wondered how she could have a baby. Gabriel explained that the Holy Spirit would come on her and the power of the Most High would make it happen, so the holy one born to her would be called the Son of God. Then Gabriel gave Mary a sign: her old relative Elizabeth, who everyone thought could not have children, was going to have a baby too. Gabriel said, "For no word from God will ever fail." Mary answered, "I am the Lord's servant. May your word to me be fulfilled." It's okay to ask God questions; Mary asked and then trusted.
dailies.enochActivity: Try to lift something too heavy, like a couch, and say, "Too hard for me!" Then point up and say, "Not too hard for God!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 36, who else was going to have a baby? Why was that surprising?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Elizabeth, Mary's relative (verse 36). It was surprising because she was old and people said she was unable to have children, but God did it.
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 35 names the Holy Spirit, the Most High, and the Son of God in one sentence. How does that connect to what we learned about one God in three persons? Is there something in your life that feels impossible right now that you could trust God with?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The Holy Spirit comes on Mary, the power of the Most High (the Father) overshadows her, and the child is the Son of God (verse 35), so all three persons are at work in Jesus' coming. Any honest answer works for the second part; the point is that God's word does not fail (verse 37).
dailies.passageText: 34 “How will this be,” Mary asked the angel, “since I am a virgin?” 35 The angel answered, “The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the holy one to be born will be called the Son of God. 36 Even Elizabeth your relative is going to have a child in her old age, and she who was said to be unable to conceive is in her sixth month. 37 For no word from God will ever fail.” 38 “I am the Lord’s servant,” Mary answered. “May your word to me be fulfilled.” Then the angel left her.

dailies.label: Day 4
dailies.focus: Hundreds of years before Mary, God promised a sign: a virgin would give birth to a son called Immanuel.
dailies.verse: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel.
dailies.enoch: Say with a parent, "God promised a baby boy, and God kept his promise!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 11, what did the LORD tell King Ahaz to ask for?
dailies.elijahAnswer: A sign. "Ask the LORD your God for a sign" (verse 11).
dailies.jordyn: Ahaz said he would not put the LORD to the test (verse 12), but Isaiah said he was trying God's patience (verse 13). Why was refusing God's offer really a lack of trust?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God himself invited Ahaz to ask for a sign (verse 11), so asking would have been obeying, not testing. Saying no sounded humble but was really refusing to trust God, which tried God's patience (verse 13).
dailies.action: Read Isaiah 7:14 and Luke 1:31 back to back. Have everyone point out what matches.
dailies.prayer: Lord, thank you for promising a sign long ago and for keeping it when Jesus came. Help us trust you instead of being afraid, like King Ahaz was. Thank you that your plans are always good and always on time. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: About 700 years before Jesus was born, Ahaz was the king of Judah, from David's family, and he was afraid of enemy kings. God sent the prophet Isaiah to tell him to trust the LORD and even to ask for a sign. Ahaz refused, saying he would not test the LORD, but really he did not want to trust God. So Isaiah said the Lord himself would give a sign anyway: the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel. When Gabriel visited Mary, a virgin from David's family, God was keeping that very promise. Next week we will learn what the name Immanuel means when an angel visits Joseph.
dailies.enochActivity: Rock a pretend baby in your arms and whisper, "Baby Jesus, God's promise!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 14, what name would the son be called? In our story about Mary, who is the son God promised?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Immanuel (verse 14). The promise came true with Jesus, the baby Gabriel told Mary she would have (Luke 1:31).
dailies.jordyn2: Compare Isaiah 7:14 with what Gabriel told Mary in Luke 1:31. What matches? How does it help your faith that God planned Jesus' birth so long before it happened?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Both say a virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and both include the child's name (Isaiah 7:14; Luke 1:27, 31). It shows Jesus' coming was God's plan all along, and that God keeps his word even across hundreds of years, so we can trust his promises to us.
dailies.passageText: 10 Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz, 11 “Ask the LORD your God for a sign, whether in the deepest depths or in the highest heights.” 12 But Ahaz said, “I will not ask; I will not put the LORD to the test.” 13 Then Isaiah said, “Hear now, you house of David! Is it not enough to try the patience of humans? Will you try the patience of my God also? 14 Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel.

dailies.label: Day 5
dailies.focus: Mary believed God would keep his promise, and God blesses those who trust his word.
dailies.verse: Blessed is she who has believed that the Lord would fulfill his promises to her!
dailies.enoch: Jump up high like Elizabeth's baby and shout, "Yay! Jesus is coming!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 39, where did Mary hurry to go?
dailies.elijahAnswer: To a town in the hill country of Judea, to Zechariah's home, to see Elizabeth (verses 39–40).
dailies.jordyn: Elizabeth called Mary "the mother of my Lord" (verse 43) before anyone told her the news. How did she know (verse 41)?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit (verse 41). God showed her who Mary's baby was, so she knew he was her Lord.
dailies.action: Challenge: Like Mary hurrying to Elizabeth, each person picks one person to encourage today with a visit, call, card, or kind word, and tells them something good about Jesus.
dailies.prayer: Lord, thank you that you always fulfill your promises. Help us believe your word even before we see it happen, like Mary did. Fill us with joy like Elizabeth's baby, and help us share good news about Jesus with someone today. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Right after Gabriel left, Mary hurried to the hill country of Judea to visit her relative Elizabeth, the one Gabriel said was going to have a baby in her old age. When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the baby inside Elizabeth leaped, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. Nobody had told Elizabeth Mary's news, but she called Mary's baby "my Lord" and said the baby inside her leaped for joy. Then she said, "Blessed is she who has believed that the Lord would fulfill his promises to her!" Mary trusted God's word before she could see it come true, and that is what faith is. Elizabeth's baby grew up to be John the Baptist, who would one day point people to Jesus.
dailies.enochActivity: Give someone in the family a happy hug or a high five, like Mary hurrying to see Elizabeth, and say, "Jesus is coming!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 44, what did Elizabeth's baby do when he heard Mary's greeting? Why do you think he did that?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He leaped for joy (verse 44). Because Mary was going to be the mother of Jesus, the Lord, and that was the happiest news ever (verse 43).
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 45 says Mary was blessed because she believed the Lord would fulfill his promises. What is one promise of God you can choose to believe this week, even before you see how it turns out?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Any promise from Scripture with a real situation works, for example that God is with us (Luke 1:28) or that no word from God will ever fail (Luke 1:37). Mary believed before she saw it (verse 45), and we can too.
dailies.passageText: 39 At that time Mary got ready and hurried to a town in the hill country of Judea, 40 where she entered Zechariah’s home and greeted Elizabeth. 41 When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. 42 In a loud voice she exclaimed: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the child you will bear! 43 But why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? 44 As soon as the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy. 45 Blessed is she who has believed that the Lord would fulfill his promises to her!”

dailies.label: Day 6
dailies.focus: Mary praised God with a song for his great things, his mercy, and his kept promises.
dailies.verse: for the Mighty One has done great things for me—holy is his name.
dailies.enoch: Sing a happy praise to God with a parent: "God does great things! Holy is his name!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 47, what does Mary call God?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "God my Savior" (verse 47).
dailies.jordyn: Verses 51–53 describe God bringing down the proud and lifting up the humble. Why do you think Mary, a young woman from a small town, sang about that?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God had chosen her, a humble servant (verse 48), not someone rich or powerful, to be Jesus' mother. She saw that God cares about the humble and lifts them up (verse 52), and that he isn't impressed by pride (verse 51).
dailies.action: Prayer time: Read Mary's song together slowly. Then each person prays one sentence of praise: "God, you are great because..."
dailies.prayer: Lord, our souls glorify you and our spirits rejoice in you, our Savior. You have done great things for us, and holy is your name. Thank you for your mercy that lasts from generation to generation and for keeping your promises. Make our hearts humble and thankful like Mary's. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: After Elizabeth blessed her, Mary burst into a song of praise. She said her soul glorifies the Lord and her spirit rejoices in God her Savior. Mary knew she was humble and ordinary, but God noticed her and did great things for her, and she said, "Holy is his name." Her song tells what God is like: his mercy lasts from generation to generation, he lifts up the humble, and he fills the hungry with good things. At the end, Mary remembers that God was keeping the promise he made to Abraham long ago. Mary even calls God "my Savior," which means she needed saving too, just like us. Today we use Mary's song to help us pray and praise God.
dailies.enochActivity: Lift your arms up high and spin slowly while saying, "God is great! I love you, God!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 49, what has the Mighty One done for Mary? Name one great thing God has done for you.
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He has done great things for her (verse 49). Any real answer works for the second part, like giving our family, keeping us safe, or sending Jesus.
dailies.jordyn2: Mary ends by saying God remembered to be merciful to Abraham, "just as he promised our ancestors" (verses 54–55). How does that tie back to last week's lesson? Which line of Mary's song would you most like to pray this week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Last week we learned that God promised a Savior long ago and always keeps his promises. Mary praises God for keeping his promise to Abraham through Jesus (verse 55). Any line with a real reason works for the second part.
dailies.passageText: 46 And Mary said: “My soul glorifies the Lord 47 and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior, 48 for he has been mindful of the humble state of his servant. From now on all generations will call me blessed, 49 for the Mighty One has done great things for me—holy is his name. 50 His mercy extends to those who fear him, from generation to generation. 51 He has performed mighty deeds with his arm; he has scattered those who are proud in their inmost thoughts. 52 He has brought down rulers from their thrones but has lifted up the humble. 53 He has filled the hungry with good things but has sent the rich away empty. 54 He has helped his servant Israel, remembering to be merciful 55 to Abraham and his descendants forever, just as he promised our ancestors.”

dailies.label: Day 7
dailies.focus: Recap: God sent Gabriel to tell Mary that Jesus, the Son of God, was coming, and Mary trusted God's word.
dailies.verse: "I am the Lord's servant," Mary answered. "May your word to me be fulfilled." Then the angel left her.
dailies.enoch: Ask, "Who visited Mary?" (An angel!) "What was the baby's name?" (Jesus!)
dailies.elijah: Name two things the angel Gabriel said about Jesus this week.
dailies.elijahAnswer: Any two: his name would be Jesus (verse 31); he would be great and called the Son of the Most High (verse 32); he would have the throne of David (verse 32); his kingdom will never end (verse 33); he would be called the Son of God (verse 35).
dailies.jordyn: This week we read Isaiah 7:14, Luke 1:26–38, and Mary's song. What does the whole week show about God's promises?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God made a promise hundreds of years earlier (Isaiah 7:14), sent Gabriel to say it was happening (Luke 1:31), and Mary praised him for keeping his word to Abraham (Luke 1:55). God never forgets, and no word from God will ever fail (Luke 1:37).
dailies.action: Read verses 37–38 together, then each person shares one thing they learned about Mary or about God this week. Next lesson: Immanuel, God with us (Joseph's dream).
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for sending Gabriel with the good news that Jesus was coming. Thank you that Jesus is the Son of God and that no word from you will ever fail. Help us be your servants like Mary, ready to trust and obey you. Get our hearts ready to celebrate Jesus this Christmas. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Today we look back at our week. God sent the angel Gabriel to Mary in Nazareth to tell her she would have a son named Jesus, who would be called the Son of the Most High and reign forever on David's throne. When Mary asked how, Gabriel said the Holy Spirit would make it happen, so the holy one born would be called the Son of God, and that no word from God will ever fail. This kept the promise God made through Isaiah long before: the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son. Mary answered, "I am the Lord's servant," visited Elizabeth, and sang a song praising God for keeping his promises. Next week, an angel visits Joseph in a dream, and we will learn what the name Immanuel means.
dailies.enochActivity: Act out the story: a parent is Gabriel and says, "You will have a baby named Jesus!" Enoch is Mary, folds his hands, and says, "Yes, God!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 38, what did Mary say back to the angel? What does that show about her?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: "I am the Lord's servant. May your word to me be fulfilled" (verse 38). It shows she trusted God and was ready to obey him.
dailies.jordyn2: Mary called herself "the Lord's servant" (verse 38). How did you say yes to God this week, and where is one place you still want to grow in trusting him?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Any honest answer works. The point is that a servant of the Lord trusts his word and obeys, even when it is hard to understand (verses 37–38).
dailies.passageText: 30 But the angel said to her, “Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favor with God. 31 You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to call him Jesus. 32 He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, 33 and he will reign over Jacob’s descendants forever; his kingdom will never end.” 34 “How will this be,” Mary asked the angel, “since I am a virgin?” 35 The angel answered, “The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the holy one to be born will be called the Son of God. 36 Even Elizabeth your relative is going to have a child in her old age, and she who was said to be unable to conceive is in her sixth month. 37 For no word from God will ever fail.” 38 “I am the Lord’s servant,” Mary answered. “May your word to me be fulfilled.” Then the angel left her.

readings.text: 18 This is how the birth of Jesus the Messiah came about: His mother Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit. 19 Because Joseph her husband was faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace, he had in mind to divorce her quietly. 20 But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. 21 She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins."

22 All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet: 23 "The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel" (which means "God with us"). 24 When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife. 25 But he did not consummate their marriage until she gave birth to a son. And he gave him the name Jesus.
14 Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel.

story: Last week we learned that the angel Gabriel visited Mary and told her she would have a baby named Jesus, the Son of God. This week we hear the other half of the story: what God told Joseph.

Joseph was the man Mary was pledged to marry, and he came from King David's family. When Joseph found out Mary was going to have a baby, he knew he was not the father. He did not know yet that the baby was from the Holy Spirit. Joseph was faithful to God's law, but he was also kind, so he planned to end the engagement quietly instead of embarrassing Mary in front of everyone.

Then God stepped in. While Joseph was asleep, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit." The angel told Joseph to name the baby Jesus, "because he will save his people from their sins." The name Jesus means that the LORD saves.

Matthew tells us this happened to keep a promise God made long ago through the prophet Isaiah, the same promise we read last week: "The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel." Immanuel means "God with us." Jesus is not just a good man sent from God; he is God himself, come to be with us.

When Joseph woke up, he did exactly what the angel of the Lord had told him. He took Mary home as his wife, and when the baby was born, Joseph gave him the name Jesus. Joseph trusted God and obeyed right away. Next week, at Christmas, we will read about the night Jesus was born and the shepherds who came to see him.
weeks.enochLine: An angel told Joseph in a dream, "Name the baby Jesus!" Jesus is God with us!
enochActivities: Activity: Dream and wake up. Enoch lies down and pretends to sleep like Joseph. A parent is the angel and whispers, "Do not be afraid! Name the baby Jesus!" Enoch jumps up and says, "Okay, God! I'll obey!"

God with us hug: a parent says, "Who is with us at home?" Enoch says, "God!" "Who is with us in the car?" "God!" "Who is with us when we sleep?" "God!" End with a big family hug and say together, "Jesus is God with us!" Paw Patrol touch: the pups are always ready to help, but Jesus is with us every single minute.
elijahQuestions: Who was Mary pledged to be married to (verse 18)?
How did the angel of the Lord talk to Joseph (verse 20)?
Why was the baby supposed to be named Jesus (verse 21)?
What does the name Immanuel mean (verse 23)?
jordynQuestions: Joseph was "faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace" (verse 19). What does that show about the kind of man Joseph was, even before the angel came?
The angel said Jesus "will save his people from their sins" (verse 21). Why is being saved from sin a bigger rescue than being saved from enemies or hard times?
Matthew says the name Immanuel means "God with us" (verse 23). How is Jesus being God with us different from God just sending a message or a helper?
weeks.jordynApplication: Joseph did not argue or put it off. "When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him" (verse 24), even though people might talk and his plans would change. God speaks to us today through the Bible. This week, when you know what God wants, like being kind, telling the truth, or obeying your parents, try doing it right away instead of later, at school, at volleyball, or at home. And when you feel alone or nervous, remember Jesus' name, Immanuel: God is with you.
elijahAnswers: Joseph (verse 18).
In a dream: "an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream" (verse 20).
Because "he will save his people from their sins" (verse 21).
"God with us" (verse 23).
jordynAnswers: He wanted to do what was right by God's law, but he was also kind and gentle. He did not want to hurt or shame Mary, so he planned to act quietly (verse 19). He loved God and cared about people.

Enemies and hard times hurt us for a while, but sin separates us from God, and we can't fix it ourselves. Jesus came to rescue us from sin itself, so we can be forgiven and belong to God forever (verse 21).
A message or helper would come from God, but Jesus is God himself who came to be with us (verse 23). God didn't stay far away; he came close, became a baby, and lived among us.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week about a time she obeyed God or a parent right away, like Joseph, and how it went. Notice and thank her when she does what is asked the first time.
weeks.prayer: Dear God, thank you for sending an angel to Joseph and for keeping your promise through Isaiah. Thank you for Jesus, who came to save us from our sins, and for being Immanuel, God with us. Help us trust you and obey right away like Joseph did. Remind us that you are always with us, at home, at school, and everywhere we go. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2
dailies.focus: God sent an angel to Joseph in a dream to tell him that Mary's baby was from the Holy Spirit and would save his people from their sins.
dailies.verse: She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.
dailies.enoch: Say with a parent, "The angel said, 'Do not be afraid!' Jesus will save us!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 20, how did the angel of the Lord appear to Joseph?
dailies.elijahAnswer: In a dream: "an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream" (verse 20).
dailies.jordyn: Joseph planned to "divorce her quietly" (verse 19). Why do you think he wanted to do it quietly instead of in front of everyone?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Joseph was faithful to the law, but he did not want to expose Mary to public disgrace (verse 19). He was kind and wanted to protect her from shame, even when he was confused and hurt.
dailies.action: Read verses 20–21 together. Each person says one thing the angel told Joseph.
dailies.prayer: Lord God, thank you for speaking to Joseph when he was worried and did not understand. Thank you that Jesus came to save us from our sins. When we feel worried or confused, help us listen to you and not be afraid. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Joseph was pledged to marry Mary, and he came from King David's family. Then he found out Mary was going to have a baby, and he knew it was not his. Joseph was faithful to God's law, but he was also kind, so he planned to end the engagement quietly so Mary would not be shamed in front of everyone. Before he did, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph son of David, do not be afraid." The angel explained that the baby was from the Holy Spirit and told Joseph to name him Jesus, "because he will save his people from their sins." Last week Mary heard the news from Gabriel; this week God made sure Joseph knew too.
dailies.enochActivity: Lie down and pretend to sleep like Joseph. When a parent whispers, "Do not be afraid!", pop up and say, "Jesus will save us!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 21, what name was Joseph supposed to give the baby? Why that name?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Jesus, because "he will save his people from their sins" (verse 21).
dailies.jordyn2: The angel called him "Joseph son of David" (verse 20). Why would that matter, remembering what Gabriel told Mary last week about David's throne (Luke 1:32)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Gabriel said God would give Jesus "the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32). Joseph was from David's family, so when he took Mary home and named Jesus, Jesus became part of David's royal family line, just as God promised.
dailies.passageText: 18 This is how the birth of Jesus the Messiah came about: His mother Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit. 19 Because Joseph her husband was faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace, he had in mind to divorce her quietly. 20 But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. 21 She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”

dailies.label: Day 3
dailies.focus: Jesus is Immanuel, which means God with us, so God is with us everywhere we go.
dailies.verse: "The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel" (which means "God with us").
dailies.enoch: Play "Is God with us?" A parent asks, "Is God with us at the park?" Enoch shouts, "Yes! Jesus is God with us!"
dailies.elijah: Game: Where is God? Take turns naming a place (school, the baseball field, the car, your bed at night). Everyone answers, "God is with us there!" Then: what does Immanuel mean in verse 23?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "God with us" (verse 23).
dailies.jordyn: Verse 22 says "All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet." What does fulfill mean here, and which promise from last week came true?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Fulfill means to make a promise come true. The promise from Isaiah 7:14, that the virgin would give birth to a son called Immanuel, came true when Jesus was born to Mary (verses 22–23).
dailies.action: Play the "Where is God?" game, then read verse 23 together and say "God with us!" in your loudest voice.
dailies.prayer: God, thank you that Jesus is Immanuel, God with us. Thank you that we are never alone, at home, at school, on the field, or in our beds at night. When we feel scared or lonely, help us remember that you are right here. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Matthew wanted his readers to know that Jesus' birth was not a surprise to God. He wrote, "All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet." That prophet was Isaiah, and the promise is the one we read last week: the virgin will give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel. Matthew tells us what Immanuel means: "God with us." That is the biggest news of Christmas. God did not just send a message from far away; in Jesus, God himself came to be with his people. Because Jesus is God with us, the people who trust him are never alone.
dailies.enochActivity: Play hide-and-seek with a parent. When you are found, shout, "God is with me everywhere!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 22, who had said this would happen long ago?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The Lord had said it "through the prophet" (verse 22). The prophet was Isaiah (Isaiah 7:14).
dailies.jordyn2: Matthew explains that the name Immanuel means "God with us" (verse 23). When is a time you might need to remember that God is with you? How could that change how you act?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Any honest answer works, like a hard test, a big game, a new place, or feeling left out. Remembering that God is with us (verse 23) can help us be brave, calm, and kind instead of afraid.
dailies.passageText: 22 All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet: 23 “The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel” (which means “God with us”).

dailies.label: Day 4
dailies.focus: Jesus came from the family of Abraham and David, just as God had planned for many generations.
dailies.verse: This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham:
dailies.enoch: Say with a parent, "Jesus is from King David's family!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 1, Jesus is called the son of which two people?
dailies.elijahAnswer: He is called "the son of David, the son of Abraham" (verse 1).
dailies.jordyn: Verse 17 counts fourteen generations, three times. What does that long family list show about God's plan for Jesus?
dailies.jordynAnswer: It shows God was working through many generations, from Abraham to David to the exile to the Messiah (verse 17). Jesus' coming was planned and carried out by God over a very long time; nothing was an accident.
dailies.action: Count to fourteen together three times, once for each part of verse 17. Then talk about one person in your own family who taught you about God.
dailies.prayer: Lord, thank you that you planned for Jesus to come for a very long time, through Abraham and David and many families. Thank you that you keep your promises from generation to generation. Help our family love and follow you, and pass our faith on to the people after us. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Matthew starts his book with a long family tree, called a genealogy. It begins, "This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham." God had promised Abraham long ago that the whole world would be blessed through his family, and he promised King David that one of his sons would rule forever. Matthew lists the generations one by one, all the way to Joseph, the husband of Mary, and Jesus, who is called the Messiah. Then he counts them: fourteen generations, three times. Messiah means the Chosen King God promised to send. Jesus' family tree shows that God kept his word, step by step, through hundreds of years.
dailies.enochActivity: Stack fourteen blocks into a tall tower and say, "God planned Jesus for a long, long time!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 16, who was Joseph's wife, and who was her son?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Mary was Joseph's wife, and her son was "Jesus who is called the Messiah" (verse 16).
dailies.jordyn2: Matthew calls Jesus "the son of David, the son of Abraham" (verse 1). Why do you think Matthew started with those two names instead of just saying Jesus was born?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God made big promises to Abraham and to David, and the Messiah was supposed to come from their families. Starting with them shows right away that Jesus is the promised one and that God kept those promises (verses 1, 17).
dailies.passageText: 1 This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham: 2 Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac the father of Jacob, Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers, 16 and Jacob the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, and Mary was the mother of Jesus who is called the Messiah. 17 Thus there were fourteen generations in all from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen from the exile to the Messiah.

dailies.label: Day 5
dailies.focus: When Joseph woke up, he obeyed God right away, and we can obey God right away too.
dailies.verse: When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife.
dailies.enoch: Play "Right away!" A parent gives a simple job, like "Touch your nose!" Enoch does it fast and says, "I obey right away, like Joseph!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 24, what did Joseph do when he woke up?
dailies.elijahAnswer: He did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife (verse 24).
dailies.jordyn: Joseph obeyed as soon as he woke up (verse 24). What might have made it hard for him to obey, and why do you think he did it anyway?
dailies.jordynAnswer: People might not understand, and his own plans had changed (verse 19). He obeyed because he trusted that God's message was true and that God's plan was good (verses 20–21, 24).
dailies.action: Challenge: Today, when a parent asks you to do something, do it the first time, right away, like Joseph. At bedtime, share one time you obeyed right away.
dailies.prayer: Lord, thank you for Joseph, who trusted you and obeyed right away. Help us hear what you say in the Bible and do it without arguing or waiting. Give us brave, willing hearts to follow you, even when it is hard. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Joseph had a big choice to make when he woke up from his dream. He could keep his old plan, or he could trust what the angel of the Lord had told him. Matthew says, "When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife." He did not argue, wait, or ask for more time. Later, when the baby was born, Joseph gave him the name Jesus, just as the angel said. The Bible praises this kind of obedience; Psalm 119:60 says, "I will hasten and not delay to obey your commands." Joseph shows us that trusting God and obeying God go together.
dailies.enochActivity: Run to a parent as fast as you can when they call your name, and say, "I'm here! I'll obey!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 25, what name did Joseph give the baby? Was that the name the angel told him?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Jesus (verse 25). Yes, it was the name the angel told him to give (verse 21).
dailies.jordyn2: Psalm 119:60 says, "I will hasten and not delay to obey your commands." What is one thing you know God wants you to do that you have been putting off? What would obeying right away look like this week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Any honest answer works, like apologizing to someone, doing chores without being reminded, or being kind to a sibling. Joseph obeyed as soon as he woke up (verse 24), and quick obedience shows we trust God.
dailies.passageText: 24 When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife. 25 But he did not consummate their marriage until she gave birth to a son. And he gave him the name Jesus.

dailies.label: Day 6
dailies.focus: At Christmas we celebrate that Jesus, the Word, became a person and came to live with us, full of grace and truth.
dailies.verse: The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.
dailies.enoch: Pray with a parent, "Thank you, God, for baby Jesus! Happy birthday, Jesus!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 14, what did the Word become?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Flesh, which means a real human person. "The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us" (verse 14).
dailies.jordyn: Verse 12 says those who receive Jesus and believe in his name get "the right to become children of God." How does that connect to the name Immanuel?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Immanuel means God with us (Matthew 1:23). Jesus came close to us (verse 14) so we could come close to God and become his children by believing in him (verse 12).
dailies.action: Prayer time: Light a candle or turn on the tree lights. Read verse 14 together, then each person thanks God for one thing about Jesus coming to us.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for sending Jesus, the Word, to become a person and live among us. Thank you that he is full of grace and truth and that everyone who receives him becomes your child. As we celebrate Christmas, fill our home with joy and help us welcome Jesus with our whole hearts. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: John tells the Christmas story in a different way from Matthew and Luke. He calls Jesus "the Word," the one through whom the whole world was made. Then he says something amazing: "The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us." That means God the Son became a real human baby and lived with people, just like the name Immanuel says. Sadly, many people did not recognize or receive him. But everyone who receives Jesus and believes in his name is given the right to become a child of God. That is the best gift of Christmas, and today we thank God for it in prayer.
dailies.enochActivity: Hold a pretend present, open it slowly, and say, "Jesus is God's best gift!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 12, what did Jesus give to all who received him and believed in his name?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He gave them "the right to become children of God" (verse 12).
dailies.jordyn2: Verses 10–11 say the world did not recognize Jesus and his own did not receive him. Why do you think people miss Jesus, even at Christmas? How can your family make room for Jesus this Christmas?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: People can be busy, distracted, or not want to change, so they miss him (verses 10–11). Any real answer works for the second part, like reading the Christmas story together, praying before opening gifts, or serving someone in need.
dailies.passageText: 10 He was in the world, and though the world was made through him, the world did not recognize him. 11 He came to that which was his own, but his own did not receive him. 12 Yet to all who did receive him, to those who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God— 13 children born not of natural descent, nor of human decision or a husband’s will, but born of God. 14 The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.

dailies.label: Day 7
dailies.focus: Recap: God told Joseph in a dream that Mary's baby was from the Holy Spirit; Jesus saves us from our sins and is Immanuel, God with us.
dailies.verse: "The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel" (which means "God with us").
dailies.enoch: Ask, "Who had a dream?" (Joseph!) "What does Immanuel mean?" (God with us!)
dailies.elijah: Name two things the angel told Joseph in his dream this week.
dailies.elijahAnswer: Any two: do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife (verse 20); the baby is from the Holy Spirit (verse 20); she will give birth to a son (verse 21); name him Jesus (verse 21); he will save his people from their sins (verse 21).
dailies.jordyn: This week we read Matthew 1, Isaiah 7:14, and John 1. What does the whole week show about who Jesus is?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Jesus is the son of David and son of Abraham God promised (Matthew 1:1), the Savior who saves his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21), and Immanuel, God with us (Matthew 1:23), the Word who became flesh (John 1:14). God planned it long ago and kept his word (Isaiah 7:14).
dailies.action: Read verses 20–23 together, then each person shares one thing they learned about Joseph or about Jesus this week. Next lesson: Christmas: Jesus is born, the shepherds.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for telling Joseph the good news and for keeping your promise through Isaiah. Thank you that Jesus saves us from our sins and that he is Immanuel, God with us. Help us trust you and obey right away like Joseph. Thank you that you are with us always. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Today we look back at our week. Joseph found out Mary was going to have a baby and planned to end their engagement quietly, but an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream. The angel said the baby was from the Holy Spirit and that Joseph should name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins. Matthew shows this kept God's promise through Isaiah, that the virgin's son would be called Immanuel, which means "God with us." When Joseph woke up, he obeyed right away. At the very end of Matthew's book, Jesus promises, "And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age." Next week we will read about the night Jesus was born and the shepherds who came to see him.
dailies.enochActivity: Act out the story: a parent is the angel and whispers in Enoch's ear while he pretends to sleep, "Name the baby Jesus!" Enoch wakes up, rocks a pretend baby, and says, "Jesus, God with us!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 24, what did Joseph do when he woke up? What does that show about him?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife (verse 24). It shows he trusted God and obeyed right away.
dailies.jordyn2: Last week Mary said, "I am the Lord's servant" (Luke 1:38), and this week Joseph obeyed as soon as he woke up (verse 24). What do Mary and Joseph teach you about trusting God, and where do you want to trust him more?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Both believed God's message and obeyed even when it was hard and people might not understand (Luke 1:38; Matthew 1:24). Any honest answer works for the second part; God is with us as we learn to trust him (verse 23).
dailies.passageText: 18 This is how the birth of Jesus the Messiah came about: His mother Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit. 19 Because Joseph her husband was faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace, he had in mind to divorce her quietly. 20 But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. 21 She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.” 22 All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet: 23 “The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel” (which means “God with us”). 24 When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife. 25 But he did not consummate their marriage until she gave birth to a son. And he gave him the name Jesus.
